summary: Ran a quick, focused test of the Writing Studio 'Save Drafts' feature. Backend: create, list, update and delete work; each project and each user only sees its own drafts; an empty title is rejected (422). UI as t1 on project FOS: generated a draft with the LLM, gave it a title and saved it, and it showed in saved-drafts-list. After an edit the button read 'Save changes' and saving updated the same draft with no duplicate. After a page reload the draft was still listed and reopened with the edited text. MD and DOCX export both downloaded. Delete (with the confirm dialog) removed the draft. Everything tested passed.

issues: Low priority: openDraft() restores only the text and title, not the saved doc_type, style or paper_ids. Export filenames come from the doc type currently selected, not the draft title (e.g. Literature_review_draft.md for 'TEST_UI draft').

action_items: Optional: when a saved draft is reopened, restore its doc_type, style and paper_ids, and use the draft title for export filenames
critical_code_review_comments: DELETE /api/drafts/{id} returns {ok:true} even when nothing matched (another user's draft or an unknown id). Nothing is deleted, but a 404 would be more consistent with PUT.
Deleting a project also deletes its drafts (server.py delete_project) - good.
seed_data_creation: Test users test_dr*@example.com and their projects are created and deleted by the pytest file. The UI test draft 'TEST_UI draft' in t1's FOS project was deleted at the end.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the drafts tests with: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_drafts_api.py -n 0. t1 has only one project (FOS), so the 'other project shows no drafts' check was done through the API, not the UI.
